correctness.rationale: The pullback characters of the polynomial monomials are indexed by (J,K,L); at fixed character the allowed x_3 exponents are exactly 0 through r=min(K,L). Since ((xi+1)/2)^2=xi t with t=|(xi+1)/2|^2, the only dependence on m after extracting the common factor is t^{-m}. Integrating against the probability arcsine law gives the stated beta matrix; independence follows on (0,1). Multiplying a vector from the predecessor character by x_3 gives precisely the span of p_1 through p_r, or zero when r=0. After extracting t^{-r}, this span corresponds to degree at most r−1 with weight t^{|K−L|−1/2}(1−t)^{J−L−1/2}. The Jacobi polynomial has exactly the required orthogonality and squared norm h_r/π in the Hardy norm. The r=0 beta convention and the (1,1,1) example check the endpoint and normalization. Multiplication by x_3 is isometric, and its nth range has no character component with K<n or L<n, so the intersection is zero and the Wold translates are complete. The frozen check.py and recorded diagnostic were inspected, not executed; the argument checks the full parameter range.
